## Background

The **Australian HR Institute (AHRI)** supports HR professionals through membership, certification, training and events.

### How incoming calls reach AHRI

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 12
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart LR
    C["`**External caller**`"] -->|"Main number"| M["`**Main IVR**
Automated menu`"]

    M -->|"Service selection"| Q["`**Team queue**
Routes calls to staff`"]

    Q -->|"Call offered"| S["`**Staff phone**`"]

    C -.->|"Direct staff number"| S

    classDef main fill:#006DAE,stroke:#006DAE,color:#ffffff,font-size:22px;
    classDef light fill:#E6F0F7,stroke:#006DAE,color:#004B7A,font-size:22px;

    class C,Q,S light;

    linkStyle 3 stroke:#7F8C97,stroke-width:2px;
```

::: callout-box
**The reporting gap:** email and online forms had CRM reporting. Phone activity was available mainly as raw Excel exports.
:::

::: muted
Illustrative routes: not every Main IVR call reaches a queue or a staff member. Our inbound analysis focuses on the main menu; outbound activity is analysed separately.
:::

::: notes
AHRI is a professional association that supports people working in human resources through membership, certification, training and events. Phone calls are one of the ways people contact AHRI about these services.

So the diagran in the middle help to show you how every calls coming to AHRI.

Imagine someone calls AHRI’s main number with a membership question. They first hear an automated menu, which we call the Main IVR. Depending on their selection, the call may enter a team queue, where the system offers it to staff.

Someone who already knows a staff member’s direct number can take a different route and call that person directly, without using the main menu.

This distinction became important when we examined the data.

AHRI already had reporting platforms for emails and online forms through CRM software. Phone activity, however, was mainly available through raw Excel exports. This created an opportunity to make that information easier to understand and use.
:::

## Business problem

:::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="55%"}
AHRI has no visibility and needs a clearer way to understand of

::: nonincremental
- **When** do members call?
- **Where** do their calls go?
- **How** do calls end, and how long do they take?
- **Who** is calling members back, and when?
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="45%"}
::: callout-box
**Our goal**

Turn the Teams phone exports into a Power BI dashboard that shows AHRI what's happening on the phones.
:::

**In scope:** inbound and outbound activity across the period of the export.<br> **Out of scope:** live reporting and individual staff performance.
::::

::: notes
The main challenge was turning those raw records into a clear picture of phone activity.

For example, when should phone coverage be strongest? Which services receive the most calls? And how much outbound calling happens across the teams?

Answering these questions from individual spreadsheet records takes time, especially when one call can produce several rows.

Our goal was to bring that information together in a dashboard that staff could explore by date, service or team.

The dashboard helps AHRI see when the phones are busiest and how call activity is spread across teams, so they can plan phone coverage.
:::
::::::::

## Business questions

|   | Question | Dashboard page |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| Inbound | How many calls arrive, and when? | Inbound Call Overview |
| Inbound | Where do callers go? | Routing and queue destinations |
| Inbound | How do calls end, and how long do they take? | Outcome and Duration |
| Outbound | Who is making outbound calls, and when? | Outbound activity |
| Outbound | How do outbound calls end, and how long do they last? | Outbound outcome and duration |

::: notes
We organised the dashboard around five questions.

For inbound activity, we wanted to understand how many calls arrive and when, where callers are routed, and what the system records about their outcomes and duration.

For outbound activity, we wanted to understand which teams make calls and when, followed by their recorded outcomes and duration.

Looking at both directions gives AHRI a broader picture of phone workload: demand arriving at the organisation and calling activity initiated by staff.

We analyse these separately because the data does not tell us whether an outbound call was a response to a particular inbound enquiry.

Each question became a dashboard page, giving the report a clear purpose and making it easier to navigate.
:::

## Data and analysis scope

Both exports cover **6 April to 1 September 2026**.

**Inbound:** one call can create several system records.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 12
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart LR
    R["`**9,859**
Inbound records`"] -->|"Group by shared ID"| G["`**6,361**
Linked call groups`"]

    G -->|"Include"| I["`**3,986**
With Main IVR`"]

    G -->|"Exclude"| D["`**2,375**
Without Main IVR`"]

    classDef source fill:#E6F0F7,stroke:#006DAE,color:#004B7A,font-size:24px;
    classDef group fill:#004B7A,stroke:#004B7A,color:#ffffff,font-size:24px;
    classDef included fill:#006DAE,stroke:#006DAE,color:#ffffff,font-size:24px;
    classDef excluded fill:#F1F3F5,stroke:#AAB3BA,color:#5F6B73,font-size:24px;

    class R source;
    class G group;
    class I included;
    class D excluded;

    linkStyle 0,1 stroke:#006DAE,stroke-width:2px;
    linkStyle 2 stroke:#7F8C97,stroke-width:2px;
```

::: {.muted style="margin-top: 0.2em;"}
Vanessa confirmed that calls without Main IVR are mostly direct to staff. We retain the 3,986 Main IVR groups and their related records. Groups do not represent unique people.
:::

::: callout-box
**Outbound scope:** 6,046 attempts by 18 approved staff across Membership, HRSC and Events.
:::

::: notes
Before calculating anything, we needed to establish what the records actually represented.

Both exports cover 6 April to 1 September 2026. The inbound file contains 9,859 system records, but one call can generate several records as it moves between phone accounts.

For example, activity at the main menu and a team queue may appear in separate rows. We grouped related rows using their shared identifier, which gave us 6,361 linked groups.

We then checked the account field, called UPN, to identify groups containing the Main IVR account. This gave us 3,986 groups.

The remaining 2,375 groups had no Main IVR record. Vanessa confirmed that these were mostly calls directly to staff. We therefore focused our inbound analysis on the Main IVR groups and their related records.

These are counts of recorded call activity. They do not represent unique people, because the same person can call more than once.

For outbound activity, we filtered the other export to outbound calls and the 18 staff approved by AHRI. That gave us 6,046 call attempts across Membership, HRSC and Events.
:::

## IDA and EDA: checking and exploring the data {#ida-eda}

::::::: {.columns style="font-size: 0.85em; display: flex; gap: 2em;"}
:::: {.column width="49%"}
### IDA · Check and prepare

::: muted
Initial data analysis · Power Query
:::

- **Inbound quality:** 334 missing account names and 785 missing start/end timestamps. Retained the rows with unknown values.
- **Scope:** grouped inbound rows by shared ID, selected Main IVR groups and filtered outbound to 18 approved staff.
- **Consistency:** cleaned account labels, set data types and converted UTC timestamps to Melbourne time.
::::

:::: {.column width="49%"}
### EDA · Explore patterns

::: muted
Exploratory data analysis · Power BI and DAX
:::

- **Timing:** compared daily, weekday, hourly and monthly activity, including a 7-day trailing average.
- **Routing and teams:** compared queue/overflow destinations and outbound volumes across teams.
- **Outcomes and duration:** examined technical statuses and duration bands. Compared mean and median to assess the effect of long calls.
::::
:::::::

::: muted
Weekday averages include zero-activity days and exclude boundary dates. Full-month comparisons cover May–August.
:::

::: notes
Once we understood the scope, we checked the data quality and explored the patterns.

The first part was initial data analysis, or IDA. This meant checking the structure, missing values, duplicates and dates before relying on the numbers.

We found 334 inbound records with missing account names and 785 with missing start and end times. We kept these records because other fields could still be useful, such as their shared identifier or recorded outcome. Missing information remained unknown.

We also found no exact duplicate inbound rows. So, grouping related records on the previous slide was different from removing duplicates.

In Power Query, we cleaned account labels, set the correct data types and converted timestamps to Melbourne time. That ensured the hourly patterns reflected local calling times.

We then moved to exploratory data analysis, or EDA, using Power BI charts and measures.

We compared activity across dates, weekdays, hours and months, then explored destinations, teams, recorded outcomes and duration.

The seven-day trailing average combines each day with the previous six days. This smooths daily fluctuations across a full week and helps us see broader changes.

For weekday averages, we included zero-activity days and excluded the first and last observed dates because they may be incomplete. Full-month comparisons covered May to August.

These checks made the comparisons more consistent. We also kept the interpretation within what the data supports: a technically successful call does not establish that someone spoke to staff or that their enquiry was resolved.
:::

# Inbound Results {background-color="#006DAE"}

::: notes
We now have a clear reporting scope, consistent preparation steps and a better understanding of what the numbers mean.

The next question is what this tells AHRI about its phone activity.

I’ll hand over to Sammi, who will start with the inbound findings—when demand is highest, where calls are routed, and what we can learn from the recorded outcomes and duration—before moving to outbound activity.
:::

## Inbound calls peak during business hours, with Tuesday the busiest day {.result}

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![Page 1 · Inbound calls overview](images/inbound1.png){.shot}
:::

::::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **Call volume:** 3,986 entries, averaging 37.4 per weekday.
- **Peak hours:** Most calls occur between 9 AM and 4 PM, declining after 5 PM.
- **Busiest day:** Tuesday (\~44 entries), compared with Friday (\~33).
- **Monthly trend:** Average weekday demand declined from \~53 in May to \~30 in August.
:::

::: callout-box
**For AHRI:** The dashboard identifies peak calling periods and demand patterns that can support staffing and phone coverage planning.
:::
:::::
:::::::

## Overflow use varies widely between services {.result}

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![](images/inbound2.png){.shot}
:::

::::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **Top demand:** Membership, Reception, Career Support get the most calls
- **Overflow:** about 1 in 4 queued calls
- **High overflow share:** Career Support (\~47%), CPD Events (\~50%)
:::

::: callout-box
**For AHRI:** The dashboard shows where calls are routed, to support routing and resourcing reviews.
:::
:::::
:::::::

## Most calls end normally, but dropped calls are the longest {.result}

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![](images/inbound3.png){.shot}
:::

::::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **Call outcome:** 97.1% success rate
- **Dropped calls:** disconnected or timed-out calls lasted longest (\~5 min)
- **Longest in queue:** Career Support (\~6.5 min on average)
:::

::: callout-box
**For AHRI:** The dashboard shows where calls spend longest in the queue. *A completed call doesn't mean the enquiry was resolved.*
:::
:::::
:::::::

# Outbound results {background-color="#006DAE"}

## The Membership team makes almost 9 in 10 outbound calls {.result}

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![](images/outbound1.png){.shot}
:::

::::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **By team:** Membership 5,275 (\~87%), HRSC 680, Events 91
- **By month:** peaked in May (77.8/weekday), dipped in June (39.0)
- **Busiest time:** Tuesday, 11am–2pm
:::

::: callout-box
**For AHRI:** shows outbound workload by team and over time. *Counts are call attempts, not staff performance.*
:::
:::::
:::::::

## 91% of outbound calls connect, most last under a minute {.result}

::::::: columns
::: {.column width="72%"}
![](images/outbound2.png){.shot}
:::

::::: {.column width="28%"}
::: takeaways
- **Connected:** 5,504 of 6,046 attempts (91%)
- **Main failure:** not answered (375 of 542)
- **Short calls:** 69% of connected calls last under 1 min (average 1:36)
:::

::: callout-box
**For AHRI:** shows how outbound calls end. *Connected may include voicemail; the data can't tell.*
:::
:::::
:::::::

::: notes
\~1.5 min. Wrap-up: "Outbound calls achieved a 91% technical success rate, with unanswered calls the main reason for failure. Most connected calls were short. Many may be voicemail, but the data can't distinguish a person from voicemail." Also on the chart: 145 rejected or busy, 22 system or network issues.
:::

## Project achievements & limitations

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
### Key achievements

::: small-list
- **Call Visibility:** 3,986 inbound calls + 6,046 outbound attempts in the dashboard
- **Business insights:** 5 business questions, one dashboard page each
- **Repeatable process:** Power Query steps re-apply to future exports
- **Interactive analysis:** filter by date, team and staff
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
### Current limitations

::: small-list
- **Inbound:** no data on whether calls were resolved
- **Outbound:** no data on whether a person or voicemail answered, or why the call was made
- **Data constraints:** limited to what Microsoft Teams exports
:::
::::
:::::::

::: callout-box
**Next step:** add answer status, abandonment and call reason to the data, to measure **service quality** alongside call activity.
:::
